clue.text: Sheep providing tufty wool

definitions.meaning: a group of sheep kept together
a tuft of wool, also the woolly material used for stuffing

explanation.surface: A farmer's sheep supply the fluffy wool for spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd of ovine animals is one sense; a matted tuft or waste fibre of wool is another.

clue.text: Anticipate trees completely

parts.note: a forest is a mass of trees
all means wholly or completely

explanation.surface: Someone foresees that the woods will be entirely gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in advance so as to prevent something is to pre-empt it.

clue.text: Beach in Nebraska

definitions.meaning: a D-Day landing beach in Normandy
the largest city of that Midwestern state

explanation.surface: Asks about a stretch of sand in a landlocked US state.
explanation.walkthrough: A beach in landlocked Nebraska is impossible; the name is shared by a Normandy D-Day beach and a Nebraskan city.
explanation.definitionFit: The US codename for a Normandy landing zone and a Midwestern city share one name.

clue.text: Field marshal employed in firing range

definitions.meaning: Lord ..., British field marshal of the First World War
a range is a cooking stove, and one employed in firing it is a kitchen worker

explanation.surface: A military commander works on a shooting range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firing range' suggests guns; here a range is a kitchen stove being fired up, and a kitchener is also an old name for a cooking range.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Kitchener was the British war minister and field marshal; a kitchen hand stokes a cooking stove.

clue.text: Facial hair gives a pretentious air to poet

parts.note: side is old slang for swagger or affected superiority
Robert Burns, the Scottish poet

explanation.surface: A man's whiskers lend a snooty manner to some versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting on side' is British slang for acting superior; Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Strips of whisker grown down the cheeks in front of the ears are a form of facial growth.

clue.text: Point to one state with impassivity

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
I is the Roman numeral one
Cal is an abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: Someone indicates a single US state calmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no feeling under hardship is being unemotional, like a Greek philosopher of that school.

clue.text: Coward to take the lead in pop

indicators.note: the word for leading role is placed inside the father word

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
to star is to take the leading role

explanation.surface: A spineless person takes the leading role in pop music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' suggests music but means father.
explanation.definitionFit: A dastard is an old word for a mean-spirited craven.

clue.text: One showing respect in the boudoir?

explanation.surface: Someone bows politely in a lady's private chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: The word read as 'bow-er' is someone who bows; rhymed with 'flower' it is a lady's private room.
explanation.definitionFit: One who bends at the waist in deference; also a poetic word for a woman's private chamber.

clue.text: Brutal, hair-raising, man-eating insect

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the word turns it upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: fur is animal hair

indicators.note: the insect swallows the man's name, holding it inside

parts.note: a fly is an insect
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A horrifying insect devours a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair-raising' looks like a description of the insect, but in a down clue 'raising' turns the hair word upside down, and 'eating' wraps the insect round the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving like a thug or bully is violent and savage.

clue.text: Fish and meat-eater

definitions.meaning: Jack ... of the nursery rhyme, who could eat no fat, only lean meat

explanation.surface: A fish and a carnivore.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Jack Sprat could eat no fat and his wife could eat no lean, so he ate the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sea fish; also the rhyme's Jack, who ate only lean flesh.

clue.text: Concomitant of Kipling's actions

parts.note: Kipling published a story collection whose title pairs Actions with a companion word, and that companion is what goes along with the actions

explanation.surface: Asks what accompanies the deeds of the writer Rudyard Kipling.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's 1909 collection was titled 'Actions and ___'; physics also pairs every action with an opposite partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Responses naturally accompany deeds, as in Kipling's book title and Newton's third law.

clue.text: Thin piece of iron used during hostilities

indicators.note: the iron symbol is placed in the middle of the word for fighting

parts.note: open hostilities are war
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A slim bit of metal was put to use in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: A biscuit or slice of something very slender, like a silicon disc, is a slim piece.

clue.text: Keep quiet about army's cache

indicators.note: the hushing word goes around the army abbreviation

parts.note: sh is the command to be silent
TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve; with the possessive S

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay silent about the military's hidden supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret hoard or hidden store of goods is a cache.

clue.text: Swiss registration with transport to Berlin used by skiers

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland
the 1948-49 Berlin Airlift flew supplies into the blockaded city

explanation.surface: A Swiss vehicle plate and the famous supply flights into Berlin are linked to skiing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Berlin Airlift supplied West Berlin by air during the Soviet blockade of 1948-49.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiers ride a cable-hung seat up the mountain slope, so the definition describes it by its users.

clue.text: Football magazine?

definitions.meaning: a magazine is a store for weapons and ammunition

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about a soccer periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' looks like a publication but means a store of munitions; Arsenal is also a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot for weapons is a military store; the North London soccer team carries the same name.

clue.text: Luxurious pub I found in Southern city>., coming up

indicators.note: the drinking place and I are placed inside
in a down clue, coming up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A plush pub turns up in a city in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses only the city word, giving YTIC, and 'found in' places the pub and I inside it, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybaris was a Greek city famed for its pleasure-loving citizens, so the adjective means self-indulgent.

clue.text: Put out of order by exploding grenade

indicators.note: an exploding object flies apart, so the letters of the bomb word scatter

explanation.surface: A bomb going off throws everything into disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploding' rearranges GRENADE.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarrange or throw into confusion is to disorder things.

clue.text: Reviving, it's more sensible to return a bit of money

indicators.note: the comparative is sent back, read from end to start

parts.note: saner means more sensible
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: Someone finds it wiser to give back a little cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses SANER to RENAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reborn or springing into life again is being revived.

clue.text: Some refreshment for team, getting three points

parts.note: a football or cricket side has eleven players
S, E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: A side gets snacks after winning three points.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack; the points are compass directions, not scores.
explanation.definitionFit: A light mid-morning snack with tea or coffee is a refreshment.

clue.text: Generous politician

explanation.surface: Describes an open-handed statesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-handed giving is one sense; a member of a centrist party is the other.

clue.text: Tract of grassland left out

parts.note: a lea is a meadow

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of place

explanation.surface: An area of meadow has been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LEFT to FLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A pamphlet or printed handout is a tract.

clue.text: Sort of brown wagon beside watercourse

indicators.note: the vehicle sits next to the channel, one after the other

parts.note: a van is a covered goods wagon
a dyke is a drainage ditch

explanation.surface: A brownish cart parked by a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: Vandyke brown is a deep brown pigment named after the painter Van Dyck.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark earthy pigment named after the Flemish painter is a shade of the colour.

clue.text: A river event confounded the old campaigner

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A riverside occasion baffles the old soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' rearranges A, R and EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An experienced ex-serviceman is an old soldier of many wars.

clue.text: Scold manager for misbehaving during race

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the race abbreviation

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: the boss is acting up, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A boss is told off for behaving badly at a racing event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' turns MANAGER into ERMAGAN, which goes 'during' TT.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrewish, nagging woman is a scold, the old noun for one who rails.

clue.text: Emperor gave America the bird early on

indicators.note: the bird comes first, placed ahead of the country

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
US is America

explanation.surface: A ruler insulted the United States from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gave the bird' suggests jeering at someone; here the bird is literal, and 'early on' puts it ahead of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman ruler of the first century AD, son of Vespasian.

clue.text: Defence -an 18 one

parts.note: 18 across is a liberal politician, abbreviated Lib
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Liberal mounts a defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 points to the answer at 18 across, here shortened to LIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of being elsewhere is a legal defence against a charge.

clue.text: Girl confusing the issue

indicators.note: to confuse something is to muddle it, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A young woman muddies the matter under discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' rearranges ISSUE; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so it stands for any young woman.

clue.text: Indian sounds like a more diminutive 23

indicators.note: signals the answer is pronounced like the shorter name

parts.note: 23 is a girl's name; a shorter pet form of it is Sue

explanation.surface: A Native American's name resembles a smaller version of a girl's.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across is SUSIE; its shorter form SUE is pronounced the same as this Plains tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people of the Great Plains, named in older usage as Indians.

clue.text: A portion of ice-cream for all

definitions.meaning: the first part of ...-frutti, a mixed-fruit ice cream
a musical direction meaning everyone plays together

explanation.surface: Someone shares a helping of ice cream with everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Tutti-frutti is an ice cream with candied fruit; in music the Italian direction marks a passage for the whole ensemble.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the first half of a fruit-studded dessert's name, and the Italian musical term for the whole orchestra.

clue.text: With taking ways

parts.note: taking ways usually means charm, but here it means a habit of taking what belongs to others

explanation.surface: Describes someone charming and winsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking ways' suggests charm; read literally it means a tendency to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieving is literally having a habit of taking things.

clue.text: Church official upset last 75% of Lancastrians

indicators.note: the letters are knocked over and rearranged
only the final nine of the twelve letters are kept, dropping the first quarter

explanation.surface: A churchman upsets most of the people of Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last 75% of' keeps the final nine of twelve letters, CASTRIANS, which 'upset' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton who looks after the sacred vessels and vestments is a church officer.

clue.text: Meal's about ten, in state

indicators.note: the afternoon meals go around the Roman numeral

parts.note: tea is a light meal; teas plural with the 's
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A meal is served around ten o'clock in some American state.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'tea' is an afternoon or early evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lone Star territory is one of the fifty US states.
